what do i actualy have to do to keep this thing working: "Section 7: Care and Cleaning — Dishwasher Model DW-60 User Manual

7.1 Cleaning the filter

The filter at the bottom of the tub catches food particles so that they are not sprayed back onto your dishes. It should be cleaned once a week, or more often if you do not rinse plates before loading them. Turn the cylindrical filter anticlockwise and lift it out, then remove the flat mesh plate underneath. Rinse both under warm running water, using a soft brush to remove any grease. Never use a metal scourer or wire brush, as this can damage the mesh. Refit the mesh plate and lock the filter by turning it clockwise until you hear a click. The dishwasher must never be used without the filter in place.

7.2 Rinse aid and salt

The rinse aid indicator on the control panel will light up when the rinse aid needs refilling, usually about once a month. Open the dispenser cap next to the detergent compartment and fill it to the MAX line, then wipe away any spills, as these can cause excess foam. If your water is hard, you will also need to add dishwasher salt to the container at the bottom of the tub when the salt indicator comes on. Use only salt made for dishwashers; table salt contains additives that may damage the water softener. When filling the salt container for the first time, add one litre of water before adding the salt.

7.3 Spray arms

Once a month, check that the holes in the upper and lower spray arms are not blocked. The lower arm can be pulled straight up; the upper arm is released by unscrewing the nut in the middle. Clear any blocked holes with a cocktail stick and rinse the arms under the tap before refitting them. Make sure both arms turn freely by hand afterwards.

7.4 Maintenance wash

To remove grease and limescale from inside the machine, run an empty maintenance wash on the 70°C programme once a month, with a dishwasher cleaner or a cup of white vinegar placed upright on the top rack. Doing this regularly also helps prevent unpleasant smells.

7.5 Outside and door seal

Wipe the door seal and the edges of the door with a damp cloth every week to remove food residue. Clean the control panel and outside of the appliance with a soft, damp cloth only; do not use sprays, bleach or abrasive cleaners, as these can mark the finish. After each cycle, leave the door slightly open for a short while to let moisture escape.

Getting there

Saltmarsh Bay wins easily here. There's a direct train from the city every hour, the journey takes 2 hours, and a return ticket cost us $48 each. In Pine Hollow we rented a wooden cabin for $140 a night. My verdict

If it's just the two of you and you don't have a car, go to Saltmarsh Bay. It's easy, relaxed, and you can do it all on foot. If you're a group of friends or a family who want peace and quiet and don't mind driving, Pine Hollow is the better choice, and splitting the cabin makes it good value. As for timing, go to Saltmarsh Bay in June before the school holidays fill it up, and save Pine Hollow for September when the trails are quiet and the evenings are still mild.

Moving out is stressful enough without a last-minute scramble. Whether you're moving across town or across the country, a bit of planning in the weeks before makes the day itself far calmer. Here's the timeline I wish someone had given me the first time I moved.

Four weeks before: give notice and book help

Check your tenancy agreement first. Most ask for at least one month's notice, and it usually has to be in writing, so send your landlord an email or letter four weeks before you plan to leave and keep a copy. Around the same time, book your removal van or movers. Good firms get booked up quickly, especially at the end of the month, and prices rise the closer you get.

Two weeks before: start packing

Get boxes, tape and a marker pen, and start with the rooms and things you use least: books, spare bedding, seasonal clothes, the stuff in the back of the cupboard. Label every box with the room it's going to, not what's in it. This is also a good moment to sell or donate anything you don't want to carry. You'll be surprised how much you can let go of.

One week before: sort out your post and bills

Set up post redirection and update your address with your bank, employer and anyone else who sends you letters. Let your energy and internet providers know your moving date so you're not paying for the old place after you leave. Many providers need at least a week's warning.

Two days before: defrost and deep clean

Switch off and defrost the fridge-freezer at least 24 hours before you move, with towels on the floor to catch the water. Then deep clean. Landlords most often take money from deposits for dirty ovens, limescale in the bathroom, and marks on the walls, so pay special attention to those. Price and setup

The R3 costs $249, which puts it firmly in the middle of the market. In the box you get the robot, a charging dock, two side brushes, a spare filter and a mopping attachment.
